```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6.5,
                      fig.height = 4, dpi = 80)
library(hyperutils)
```

Before a model is built or a non-compartmental analysis is run, the data
should be looked at. This vignette takes the example dataset through the
exploratory workflow of the package: prepare the data, describe it, draw the
standard figures, and write each of them to disk.

## Step 1: prepare the dataset

`hp_eda_prepare()` is the only step that touches the raw data. It returns an
object with two frames.

```{r prepare}
d <- hp_read_data(hp_example_file())
e <- hp_eda_prepare(d, dvid = "DVID", lloq = 0.5, color = "DOSEGRP")
e
```

The **record frame** (`e$rec`) has one row per record and adds the derived
columns that the plots need: time after the latest dose (`TAD`), time after
the first dose (`TAFD`), the latest dose (`DOSE`), the dose-normalised
observation (`DVNORM`), the BLQ flag (`BLQ`), the record type (`EVENT`) and
whether an observation is a concentration (`PKOBS`).

The **subject frame** (`e$subj`) has one row per individual with the baseline
covariates, the counts of records and the observed exposure (`CMAX`, `TMAX`,
`AUCLAST` and others).

```{r frames}
names(e$rec)
head(e$subj[, c("ID", "DOSE1", "NOBS", "NBLQ", "CMAX", "TMAX", "AUCLAST", "WT")])
```

The covariates are found from the data. Override them with the `continuous`,
`categorical` and `time_varying` arguments when the guess is wrong.

```{r covariates}
e$info$continuous
e$info$categorical
```

## Step 2: describe the dataset with tables

A table is described by a specification built with `hp_eda_tspec()` and
computed with `hp_eda_table()`. Three kinds exist: `summary` (descriptive
statistics), `count` (counts and percentages) and `listing` (rows).

```{r data-summary}
hp_eda_data_summary(e)
```

```{r cov-table}
hp_eda_table(e, hp_eda_tspec(
  kind = "summary", scope = "subjects", vars = c("WT", "AGE"),
  by = "DOSEGRP", overall = TRUE,
  stats = c("n", "mean", "sd", "median", "min", "max")))
```

```{r count-table}
hp_eda_table(e, hp_eda_tspec(kind = "count", scope = "subjects",
                             vars = "SEX", by = "DOSEGRP", overall = TRUE))
```

Missing values and correlations between covariates are checked the same way:

```{r missing}
head(hp_eda_missing(e), 5)
hp_eda_correlation(e)
```

A listing of rows can answer a specific question. This one lists the
observations below the limit of quantification:

```{r listing}
hp_eda_table(e, hp_eda_tspec(
  kind = "listing", scope = "obs", vars = c("ID", "TIME", "DV", "BLQ"),
  filter = "BLQ == 1", max_rows = 8))
```

## Step 3: draw figures

A figure is described by a specification built with `hp_eda_spec()` and
drawn with `hp_eda_plot()`. The function returns a list of ggplot objects, one
per page.

### Individual concentration-time profiles

```{r spaghetti}
units <- list(time = "h", conc = "ng/mL", dose = "mg")
spaghetti <- hp_eda_spec(name = "spaghetti", title = "Individual profiles",
                         kind = "line", x = "TAFD", y = "DV", color = "DOSEGRP",
                         pk_only = TRUE, log_y = TRUE)
hp_eda_plot(e, spaghetti, units)[[1]]
```

### Typical profile with a spread

A `summary` plot bins the x variable and draws a centre and an error bar for
each bin by colour group.

```{r summary-plot}
typical <- hp_eda_spec(name = "typical", title = "Median and quartiles",
                       kind = "summary", x = "TAFD", y = "DV", color = "DOSEGRP",
                       centre = "median", spread = "iqr", pk_only = TRUE,
                       log_y = TRUE)
hp_eda_plot(e, typical, units)[[1]]
```

### Dose proportionality by eye

Dose-normalised concentrations from different dose groups should overlap when
the exposure is dose proportional.

```{r dose-norm}
dn <- hp_eda_spec(name = "dosenorm", title = "Dose-normalised concentration",
                  kind = "summary", x = "TAFD", y = "DVNORM", color = "DOSEGRP",
                  centre = "geomean", spread = "sd", pk_only = TRUE, log_y = TRUE)
hp_eda_plot(e, dn, units)[[1]]
```

### Covariate against exposure

With `scope = "subjects"` the plot uses the subject frame, which holds the
observed exposure.

```{r cov-exposure}
cov_plot <- hp_eda_spec(name = "wt_cmax", title = "Cmax against body weight",
                        kind = "scatter", scope = "subjects", x = "WT", y = "CMAX",
                        color = "DOSEGRP", smooth = "linear")
hp_eda_plot(e, cov_plot, units)[[1]]
```

### Distributions

```{r hist}
hist_plot <- hp_eda_spec(name = "wt_hist", title = "Body weight",
                         kind = "histogram", scope = "subjects", x = "WT",
                         hist_bins = 8)
hp_eda_plot(e, hist_plot, units)[[1]]
```

Several variables in `x` draw one panel per variable:

```{r box}
box_plot <- hp_eda_spec(name = "box", title = "Exposure by dose group",
                        kind = "box", scope = "subjects", x = "DOSEGRP",
                        y = c("CMAX", "AUCLAST"), free = "y")
hp_eda_plot(e, box_plot, units)[[1]]
```

### One panel per individual

Facet by `ID` and the figure is split into pages of `ncol * nrow` panels:

```{r pages}
panels <- hp_eda_spec(name = "individual", title = "Individuals", kind = "line",
                      x = "TAFD", y = "DV", facet = "ID", pk_only = TRUE,
                      log_y = TRUE, ncol = 4, nrow = 3)
pages <- hp_eda_plot(e, panels, units)
length(pages)
pages[[1]]
```

## Step 4: save everything

`hp_save_plots()` writes every page (numbered when there are several) and
`hp_save_table()` writes a table as a CSV file. Both need a folder.

```{r save}
out <- file.path(tempdir(), "eda")
f1 <- hp_save_plots(pages, "individual", out, width = 9, height = 7, dpi = 72)
f2 <- hp_save_table(hp_eda_data_summary(e), "data_summary.csv", out)
basename(c(f1, f2))
unlink(out, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Choosing the right plot

| Question | Plot |
|----------|------|
| Are the profiles plausible, any outliers? | `line`, log y axis |
| What is the typical profile and its spread? | `summary` |
| Is exposure dose proportional? | `summary` of `DVNORM` by dose group |
| Does a covariate relate to exposure? | `scatter`, `scope = "subjects"`, `smooth` |
| How are covariates distributed? | `histogram`, `box`, `bar` |
| Are covariates correlated? | `corr` or `pairs` |
| How does the effect follow concentration? | `pkpd` (needs a `DVID` for each) |
